Three-panel academic figure for a top-venue NLP paper (EMNLP), full width, aspect ratio ~3.2:1, figsize (14, 4.5) inches, 300 DPI.

This figure compares three execution-free verification formulations for code repair. Each panel shows one formulation as Input → Model → Output flow.

LAYOUT: Three equal-width panels side-by-side, separated by generous whitespace (wspace=0.4). Each panel has a subtle colored header bar at the top with the formulation name.

PANEL (a) "CLS — Classification" (left, ~33% width):
- Header bar: steel blue (#3274A1), rounded top corners 8px
- Below header: a vertical flow diagram
- INPUT BOX (top): light gray (#F5F6F7) rounded rect (8px corners), thin border (#DEE2E6), containing:
  - Title in bold: "Code + Test"
  - Subtitle in gray 8pt: "per-test input"
- ARROW: thin gray (#AAAAAA) arrow pointing down, elegant arrowhead
- MODEL BOX (middle): white rounded rect with thin steel blue (#3274A1) border, containing:
  - "LoRA Model" in center, 10pt
  - Small brain/gear icon or just text
- ARROW: thin gray arrow pointing down
- OUTPUT BOX (bottom): steel blue (#3274A1) fill with white text, rounded rect:
  - "PASS / FAIL" in bold white, 11pt
  - Below in lighter blue: "1 token"
- ANNOTATION below: "Per-test granularity" in gray italic 8pt
- Small green checkmark ✓ badge near output: "diagnostic"

PANEL (b) "CWM — Code World Model" (center, ~33% width):
- Header bar: burnt orange (#E1812C), rounded top corners 8px
- INPUT BOX (top): same style as CLS, containing:
  - Title: "Code + Test"
  - Subtitle: "per-test input"
- ARROW down
- MODEL BOX (middle): white rounded rect with orange (#E1812C) border:
  - "LoRA Model" in center
- ARROW down
- OUTPUT BOX (bottom): TWO STACKED boxes:
  - Top sub-box: orange (#E1812C) fill, white text:
    - "Execution Output" in bold
    - "O(L) tokens" below in lighter orange
  - Arrow pointing right to a small comparison box
  - Comparison sub-box: light orange background:
    - "≟ Expected" in dark text
    - "exact match" in 8pt gray
- ANNOTATION below: "Per-test granularity" in gray italic 8pt
- Small red ✗ badge near output: "format collapse at repo level"

PANEL (c) "TRAJ — Trajectory" (right, ~33% width):
- Header bar: forest green (#3A923A), rounded top corners 8px
- INPUT BOX (top): same style, BUT TALLER/WIDER to emphasize more input:
  - Title: "Full Patch + All Tests"
  - Subtitle: "patch-level input"
  - Maybe a small stack icon or multiple document icon to show it takes ALL tests
- ARROW down
- MODEL BOX (middle): white rounded rect with green (#3A923A) border:
  - "LoRA Model" in center
- ARROW down
- OUTPUT BOX (bottom): green (#3A923A) fill with white text:
  - "RESOLVED / UNRESOLVED" in bold white
  - "1 token" below in lighter green
- ANNOTATION below: "Patch-level granularity" in gray italic 8pt

KEY VISUAL DISTINCTIONS TO EMPHASIZE:
- The OUTPUT section heights should differ visually: CLS and TRAJ have compact 1-token outputs, CWM has a taller multi-step output (generation + comparison)
- CWM's output box should be noticeably taller/more complex than the other two
- The input box for TRAJ should be wider/taller than CLS/CWM to show it takes more input
- Use consistent vertical alignment across all three panels for the Model box

OVERALL STYLE:
- 300 DPI, white background, publication quality for EMNLP 2025
- Elegant, premium, sophisticated — NOT cheap or homework-like
- Serif font (Times New Roman or similar) for main labels
- Sans-serif (Helvetica) for annotations and subtitles
- Panel labels '(a)', '(b)', '(c)' in 11pt bold at top-left of each panel
- Subtle drop shadows (2px offset, 10% opacity) on all boxes
- Rounded corners 8px on all rectangles
- Arrow heads: small, elegant, not bulky matplotlib defaults
- Muted, harmonious color palette — NO saturated primary colors
- Generous white space between elements
- Consistent visual weight across all panels
- NO matplotlib default styling: no gray background, no thick gridlines, no tab10 colors
- All text must be readable at column width (~3.5 inches per panel when printed)

We present the first systematic empirical comparison across two representative code LLM families (Qwen3, DeepSeek-Coder), two complexity levels (function-level and repository-level), and multiple seeds. Our contribution is primarily methodological: a matched experimental framework that controls for major confounding variables. The analysis also produces actionable outputs: a failure mode taxonomy that characterizes when and why each formulation fails (\S\ref{sec:repo}), error complementarity findings with practical ensemble implications (\S\ref{sec:analysis}), and formulation selection observations conditioned on code complexity (\S\ref{sec:conclusion}). The results suggest a three-layer structure. Fine-tuning is necessary (0-shot$\to$fine-tuned gains of 35--36 percentage points (pp) at repo level). After fine-tuning under our ${\leq}$8B LoRA protocol, \emph{formulation choice is moderated by code complexity, operating through output format}: function-level outputs average ${\sim}$5--15 tokens (minimizing generation-specific failures per \S\ref{sec:failure-modes}), while repo-level outputs average ${\sim}$477 tokens (triggering format collapse): at function level, all formulations achieve comparable accuracy, consistent with the theoretical analysis in \S\ref{sec:failure-modes}, which predicts that short outputs minimize generation-specific failures. At repository level under our ${\leq}$8B LoRA protocol, this equivalence diverges; variant-level analysis identifies three distinct failure modes consistent across model families, though gap magnitude depends on multiple confounds (\S\ref{sec:threats}). Figure~\ref{fig:reformulation} illustrates the three formulations.

We make the following contributions:

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Complexity-moderated formulation choice.} We establish a three-layer structure: (1)~fine-tuning is necessary (35--36\pp{} gains); (2)~at function level, formulations are near-equivalent: \cls{} and \cwm{} achieve statistical equivalence (TOST $p{=}0.007$, Holm-corrected, Qwen3 5 seeds; DeepSeek directionally consistent, 2 seeds), while \traj{} equivalence is inconclusive after Holm correction, but the gap narrows from 3.11\pp{} at 4B to 1.07\pp{} at 14B (\S\ref{sec:scaling}); (3)~at repository level under ${\leq}$8B LoRA, this equivalence diverges ($z{=}-23.7$, DeepSeek-Coder), with \cwm{} falling 18--26\pp{} below \cls{}, accompanied by format collapse; four interventions all fail to close the gap. The TOST framework demonstrates strict equivalence rather than mere non-significance. Error analysis reveals partially complementary patterns (oracle: 90.63\% function, 95.83\% repo), though simple heuristics capture $<$0.4\pp{}, framing ensemble routing as an open challenge (\S\ref{sec:equivalence}, \S\ref{sec:repo}, \S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\item \textbf{Failure mode taxonomy.} Variant-level analysis identifies three distinct failure modes at repository level, namely format collapse (\cwm{}), decision collapse (\cls{} under truncate preprocessing), and aggregation penalty (\cls{} under all-pass rule), providing actionable diagnostic criteria for practitioners selecting a verification formulation (\S\ref{sec:repo}, Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy}).
\end{itemize}

Our central finding is that \emph{code complexity moderates the classification--generation tradeoff}: at function level, all formulations achieve comparable accuracy; at repository level, this equivalence breaks down as generation-based verification suffers format collapse. \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Complexity-moderated equivalence and divergence.} At function level, classification and generation are statistically equivalent; at repository level, generation accuracy drops sharply due to output format complexity, while classification and trajectory scoring remain competitive (\S\ref{sec:equivalence}, \S\ref{sec:repo}).

\end{itemize}
